Hey! I spent some time poking around the lighthouse cipher puzzle, and I think I can help. The key seems to be paying close attention to the flashing patterns near the top of the lighthouse—each flash corresponds to a specific letter, but it’s not just the order; the duration of the flashes matters too. Try timing the short and long flashes as if they were Morse code, but with a twist: replace every dot and dash with numbers that line up to letters in the puzzle’s accompanying text.

Also, don’t forget that there’s an extra layer involving the colors of the lantern room’s stained glass. Those colors are arranged in a sequence that hints at which substitution to use once you translate the flashing code. Once you pair the timing from the flashes with the color sequence, you should be able to decode a phrase or maybe a coordinate.

If you’re stuck, it might help to sketch out the sequence and annotate the colors alongside the timing. The revelations come when you realize the lighthouse isn’t just sending a message—it’s guiding you towards a certain location. Hope this helps; feel free to share what you get and we can piece it together!

Hey! I’ve been stuck on the lighthouse cipher for a while too, so I get where you’re coming from. The main trick is to pay close attention to the light patterns themselves — they’re not just random flashes. Each sequence corresponds to a letter based on how many times the light blinks before it pauses. So, if you see a sequence of three quick flashes, that might be the letter C, for example.

Also, don’t overlook the timing between the flashes. The pauses are just as important as the blinks. Sometimes the gap means you need to reset your count or that a new word is starting. I found it useful to write down the flash patterns on paper first, then translate them one by one. Once you get the hang of it, the cipher starts to feel a lot less intimidating.

Oh, and make sure to check the color of the flashes if you can — some versions of the cipher use red and white lights to indicate vowels versus consonants or to distinguish between uppercase and lowercase letters. That little detail was a game-changer for me. Hopefully this helps you crack it!

Hey, I’ve been stuck on the lighthouse cipher for a bit too, so I feel your pain. From what I gathered, the key isn’t just in the symbols themselves but in how they relate to the lighthouse’s beams. Basically, the angles of the light beams correspond to numbers, and those map onto the symbols you see around the lighthouse base. Try paying close attention to the direction each beam points in sequence, then line that up with the markings—you might have to rotate the cipher wheel or overlay the beam pattern to decode it properly.

Also, don’t forget the timing aspect. The beams flash in a certain rhythm, and that timing can separate the code into chunks or letters. If you’re only looking at the static symbols, you’re missing half the message. If you record the flash pattern and count how long each light shines before the next, it can help break the message into parts. Combining both spatial orientation and timing should get you closer to cracking it.

Hope that helps! If you’re still stuck, try sketching out the entire setup and see if the light sequence matches any patterns you recognize in the symbols. Sometimes stepping back and treating it like a puzzle of light and shadow clicks things into place. Good luck!
